about.title: How Karma weighs your day
about.p1: Karma reads what you share and finds your deliberate actions. Each one is marked Punya (merit) or Paap (a growth area) and given points from 1 to 50.
about.p2: The points are not fixed. They depend on the act, your intention, the effort or sacrifice, and who was helped or hurt, weighed against principles from Hindu dharma: the Gita, the Mahabharata, the Upanishads, the Puranas and the ten marks of dharma in Manusmriti.
about.p3: Two similar acts can score differently: help given quietly scores more than help given for show, and accidental harm scores far less than deliberate harm. Ordinary routine such as commuting or meals is not scored.
about.p4: The AI picks the exact number inside the range of the principle it matches (listed below) and shows that principle next to each act. It runs at temperature 0 with a strict format. It never invents verses: any teaching shown comes from a curated list stored in the app. The ranges are our own guide and are open to review by scholars.
about.p5: Each pot fills at 100 points for a day (week ×7, month ×30). Lifetime uses a log scale. Karma is a mirror for reflection, not a judgment of you, and gives no religious ruling, legal, medical or financial advice.
about.panchang: The tithi shown on Home is computed on your device (Lahiri ayanamsa, amanta months, Gujarati calendar). Adhik months are not marked separately.
